claims_to_fix.statement: TUFM is the only pool gene with significant, replicated gut MR: higher expression in sigmoid colon raises UC risk, odds ratio per SD [gene=TUFM; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=colon_tissue; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.191], colocalising with the IBD GWAS and replicating in FinnGen and Liu 2023. In IBDverse plasma B cells the odds ratio per SD is [gene=TUFM; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.356], also colocalising and replicating, so inhibition is the therapeutic direction. It has a single instrument (Steiger direction correct; Egger and weighted median not computable), no plasma pQTL, and the Open Targets association is outside the top 150 of the graph.

claims_to_fix.statement: The genetic-target record gives a fine-mapped UC signal (tier confident) whose risk allele raises TUFM expression, predicted mainly in blood neutrophil and colon myeloid cells; biopsies show no change, and the single-cell cell family is epithelial, which does not match the predicted cell. TUFM is a mitochondrial elongation factor, so a drug route is unclear (no clinical drug).

claims_to_fix.statement: CFB has an approved inhibitor for IgA glomerulonephritis and paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, none tried in UC or IBD. It is not loss-constrained, with no curated safety events, but it has no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL (MR not tested, which is not evidence against it); the pool dossier flags a red safety light for CFB (vital-organ expression, complement deficiency on loss).

claims_to_fix.statement: LY96 (MD-2) has a phase 3 inhibitor in sepsis and covid-19 and none in UC. Plasma MR (two instruments) is not significant and does not replicate in FinnGen; gut cell MR (non-classical monocytes) is also not significant. MGI records no colitis phenotype, although the pool lists two mouse-colitis papers that call MD-2/TLR4 blockade beneficial.

claims_to_fix.statement: CHI3L1 changes strongly in biopsies, but its genetics do not support it: plasma MR is not significant and does not replicate in FinnGen, and colon-tissue MR is also not significant. The literature is split between pathogenic and protective mouse results (knockout worsens colitis), so inhibition has a possible mucosal-protection risk.

SERPINB5 has two independent mouse colitis papers in which knockdown or ablation protects (pathogenic role), the strongest in-vivo support among the pool genes in the known list, and it is intrinsically epithelial. It has no genetic instrument, so human genetics are untested.

claims.claim: the strongest in-vivo support among the pool genes in the known list
